steps.title: Pull supporting notes from the records
steps.detail: Pulled 7 relevant items from the records (visits, results, medicines). Nothing is added that isn't on file.

steps.title: Get a letter of medical necessity from the doctor
steps.detail: Called Harbor Light Internal Medicine at (555) 010-0211: pressed 4 (medical records), then transferred to the doctor's medical assistant, waited 15 minutes on hold, reached Rob, the doctor's medical assistant. steps.title: Match the evidence to the plan's rules
steps.detail: Mapped 16 pieces of evidence to the plan's 4 rules: 4 met, 0 partly.

steps.title: Stress-test the appeal
steps.detail: Stress-tested: the insurer-side reviewer went over it 2 times; the writer answered its objections in 1 revision, and the last review found no reason to deny.

steps.title: Fax it to the plan and confirm it arrived

objections.reason: The appeal letter does not argue homebound status or cite the 2026-10-10 PT evaluation showing leaving home requires a walker, help, and taxing effort.

objections.needs: Explain in the letter why home PT is reasonable and necessary for this condition and cite the 2026-10-14 doctor's note about outpatient safety risk

revision.body:
Dear Appeals Unit at Bluewater Health,

I am appealing the denial of home health physical therapy, which was denied because the plan says it isn't medically necessary. My member ID is BWM-77031882.

My doctor, Dr. Samuel Okafor (Harbor Light Internal Medicine), has written the enclosed letter of medical necessity. The enclosed records show the history behind the request. Each of the plan's coverage criteria is answered in the enclosed table, and summarized here:

1. The member is homebound: leaving home takes a considerable and taxing effort. The 2026-10-10 physical therapy evaluation shows I need a walker and one person's help to leave home, and that leaving home takes a taxing effort.

2. A doctor has certified a plan of care for the therapy. Dr. Samuel Okafor certified and signed the 2026-10-14 home health plan of care for physical therapy, 12 visits.

3. Skilled therapy is needed to restore or keep the member's function. The 2026-10-10 physical therapy evaluation finds my balance and walking have declined since the fall, and skilled therapy can restore them.

4. The services are reasonable and necessary for the member's condition. Home therapy is reasonable and necessary because the 2026-10-14 doctor's note states outpatient therapy isn't safe for me right now because of fall risk on stairs and in transit, and the evaluation and certified plan support restoring balance and walking at home.

Please send me the plan's decision in writing, and a copy of the criteria used.
